one_month_reasoning: No Dycom earnings fall inside the window to 2026-11-08: Q3 FY2027 (quarter ends Oct 31) should report in late November (the prior-year Q3 was released 2025-11-19, src 12, 7). Events in the window are read-throughs and macro: (1) late-October Q3 reports and capex commentary from Dycom's big customers (AT&T 20.1% and Verizon 10.4% of Q2 revenue, src 3) plus Charter/Comcast/Lumen; (2) peer reports from MasTec/Quanta in late Oct/early Nov; (3) hyperscaler capex guidance in late October, which drives the AI-infrastructure contractor group; (4) the Oct 27-28 FOMC, where Kalshi/Polymarket price ~16% odds of a 25bp hike and ~84% hold (snapshot 2026-10-11, volume not shown; src 26). None is a clear directional signal. The stock is at its 52-week low after a -2.9% day on Oct 9 (src 27) and had traded $290 on Oct 7 (src 10), so both continued-momentum and short-term-reversal effects are in play and roughly cancel. I therefore use a near-symmetric lognormal centred on ~$269.5 with monthly sigma ~15% (52% annual / 3.5).

fair_value.method: Blend of NTM adjusted P/E ($21.5 NTM EPS at Oct-2027 x 15.5x = $333, 45%), FY28 EV/EBITDA ($1,245M x 10x less ~$2.2B net debt over 30.4M shares = $337, 35%) and FY28 FCF yield ($17.7/share at 6% = $294, 20%) gives ~$327.

inputs_detail.derivation: Consistent with H1 actual $9.71 (src 1) + Q3 guide midpoint $4.56 (src 1) + Q4 consensus ~$2.83 (src 13).

$20.78 x 1.12. 12% growth chosen below consensus FY28 revenue growth (+13%: $8.58B vs $7.58B, src 13) and below the 3Y EPS growth forecast of 27.3% (src 14) because H2 FY27 Communications revenue is implied roughly flat (see key uncertainties); backlog $12.24B +53% and next-12-month backlog $6.47B (src 2) support continued growth.
0.25 x $20.78 + 0.75 x $23.27 = $22.65, haircut ~5% for risk that Communications re-acceleration in FY28 disappoints = $21.5.

Peer forward P/E median 22.9x, range 15.2x-38.3x (src 15-25); DY trades at 14.6x today (src 14). 15.5x sits at the bottom of the peer range: discount for (a) adjusted EPS that excludes intangible amortization only since Q4 FY26 (src 7) - Q2 GAAP EPS $3.81 vs adjusted $5.29 (src 1); (b) customer concentration AT&T+Verizon+Lumen 35.8% of Q2 revenue (src 3); (c) leverage, notional net debt $2.50B (src 2).

methods.name: EV/EBITDA
methods.inputs: FY28 adj. EBITDA $1,245M (rev $8.58B x 14.5%) x 10.0x = EV $12.45B; less net debt ~$2.2B; / 30.4M diluted shares

inputs_detail.derivation: H1 FY27 margin 14.6% (src 2); Q3 guide midpoint $291.5M / $1.94B = 15.0% (src 1); FY26 13.3% (src 6); held near H1 level given guided slight Communications margin decline (src 2) offset by Building Systems high-teens to low-20s.

DY today: EV $10.82B (src 14) / FY27 EBITDA ~ $1.09B (H1 $578M src 1 + Q3 guide mid $291.5M src 1 + Q4 ~ $216M = implied Q4 revenue ~$1.66B at ~13%) = ~10x. Peer trailing EV/EBITDA median 17.3x, range 11.0x-36.9x (src 15-25); 10x forward ~ 11.5x trailing, at the low end of the peer range for the reasons in the P/E method.

Notional net debt $2,502.6M at Aug 1 2026 (src 2); FY26 FCF $435.3M with H2-weighted seasonality (src 6, H1 FY27 FCF -$54.2M src 2) suggests ~$500M FCF over the next ~14 months, less ~$200M for tuck-in M&A/buybacks (new $150M authorization and active M&A, src 4).

methods.name: FCF yield
methods.inputs: FY28 FCF ~ $537M (85% of adj. NI $632M) = $17.7/share at a 6.0% yield

inputs_detail.derivation: FY26 FCF $435.3M (src 6); TTM FCF $468.7M (src 14); adjusted NI now excludes ~$60M/quarter amortization (src 1) and growth ties up working capital (DSO 101 days, src 2), so conversion is set below 100%.
Current TTM FCF yield $468.7M / $8.12B market cap = 5.8% (src 14); 6% reflects leverage and rate-hike risk (src 26).

bear.story: Communications stays flat-to-down into FY28 (H2 FY27 implied ~flat ex-deferral), wireless deferral slips again, BEAD construction delayed, AI/hyperscaler capex cools and rate hikes pressure contractor multiples; FY28 EPS ~$17 x ~11x.

base.story: FY28 guide (Mar-2027) near consensus with Communications re-accelerating on the $150M wireless catch-up, BEAD construction and >$1B long-haul backlog; Building Systems grows; NTM EPS ~$21-22 at ~14x as the market keeps a concentration/amortization discount.

bull.story: Backlog conversion ($12.2B, +53%) drives beats and a strong FY28 guide, FCF de-levers balance sheet, multiple re-rates toward ~20x NTM EPS (still below peer median 22.9x).

comps_summary.our_multiple_vs_peers: 15.5x NTM adjusted P/E is at the bottom of the peer range and ~32% below the median; 10x forward EV/EBITDA (~11.5x trailing-equivalent) is also at the low end. DY today: 14.6x forward P/E, 11.6x trailing EV/EBITDA (src 14).
comps_summary.premium_discount_justification: Discount is structural and persists through the horizon: (1) quality of earnings - adjusted EPS has excluded intangible amortization only since Q4 FY26 (src 7) and the add-back is large (Q2 amortization $60.5M pre-tax; GAAP EPS $3.81 vs adjusted $5.29, src 1), so the headline P/E flatters relative to DY's own history; (2) customer concentration - AT&T 20.1%, Verizon 10.4%, Lumen 5.3% of Q2 revenue (src 3) and AT&T 25.4%/Verizon 14.0%/Lumen 10.8% in FY26 (src 8); (3) leverage - notional net debt $2.50B, ~2.3x pro forma (src 2, 4) after the $1.95B Power Solutions deal; (4) organic growth slowing from 24.7% in Q1 to 16.7% in Q2 and implied roughly flat Communications revenue in H2 FY27 (src 5, 1). Against that, DY's 3Y EPS growth forecast (27.3%, src 14) is near the peer middle, which is why I stay inside the range rather than below it.

thesis_break_reason: $200 is ~9.6x FY28 consensus EPS of $20.78 (src 13) and ~26% below today; trading there would most likely mean the market is pricing a real earnings reset (FY28 guide well below consensus, a major customer cutting fiber/wireless capex, or Building Systems margins collapsing from 24.5%) or a balance-sheet problem at ~2.3x leverage, not ordinary volatility.

reasoning: Dycom (Dycom Industries) has fallen from a $566.47 52-week high to $269 (near the 52w low of $263.36; src 27), ~13x FY28 consensus adjusted EPS, while reported fundamentals kept improving: FY27 revenue guide raised from $6.85-7.15B (Mar) to $7.48-7.66B (Aug), Q2 adj. EPS $5.29 vs ~$4.68 consensus, backlog $12.24B (+53%). Reading the filings rather than recaps shows why the market derated: (1) organic growth is decelerating fast (24.7% Q1, 16.7% Q2, Q3 guide implies mid-single digits) and the guide implies roughly flat Communications revenue in H2 FY27, with a $150M wireless deferral and a cut to the Communications range ($6.03-6.20B to $5.90-6.01B) masked by Building Systems; (2) the margin message flipped from 'modest improvement' (May) to 'slight decline' for Communications; (3) adjusted EPS now excludes ~$60M/quarter of amortization, so P/Es are not comparable with history; (4) leverage ~2.3x and H1 FCF negative. Against that, backlog, DSO improvement (101 days), new $150M buyback and a sell-side consensus target of ~$521 (src 14) argue the selloff overshot. Insider filings in October are only a tax withholding and a departing director's 1,000-share sale: no signal. My fair value blends P/E, EV/EBITDA and FCF yield at the low end of an 11-company peer set (median 22.9x fwd P/E) to ~$327 (+21%). For the ladder I shrink toward the market because the downtrend, a likely December rate hike, and the possibility of FY28 consensus cuts are real, so I centre the 12-month distribution at ~$292 median (mean ~$315) with a lognormal sigma ~0.47 (realized vol 52% but some of that was a one-way derating), and a slightly fatter left tail. P(>=269) ~0.57. Scenarios: bear $190 (25%), base $305 (50%), bull $450 (25%). Source mix: 12 of 28 sources are primary filings/transcripts; the 11 peer-multiple pages required by the comps rule are data sources outside my lane, so the in-lane share falls below 60% overall (12 of 17, 71%, excluding the comps pages). Sec.gov refused scripted access with a generic UA, so filings were read with WebFetch; the company IR site returned 403; Twelve Data statistics/targets were paywalled and not used; no option data was consulted.
